doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Piano lessons, then taking up saxophone
summary: Piano from seven to eleven, quit after a teacher said everything was wrong; at twelve or thirteen an uncle gave him a Selmer and he played a gig the next night.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Was the saxophone your first choice of instruments?

I started playing piano when I was seven and I had lessons ‘til the age of eleven and then I stopped because I changed teacher and the teacher basically said well you’re doing everything incorrectly, you know your posture is wrong, your hand position is wrong, your timing is wrong. We’re going to start again from the beginning and I wasn’t having any of that. So I gave up the piano and at the age of twelve, thirteen, I just thought I want to play the saxophone. And my uncle brought round the sort of cheap Selmer and showed me what to do on the Friday night, and on the Saturday night I played the gig.
Aw come on. You can’t make this stuff up.
Well I already played the recorder you see.
Okay so you had sort of a sense.
Where one’s fingers went you know. But I can’t even imagine what I played. I think “Green Onions” in the key of — concert key of E you know was about the limit I could manage.
